answer: Split each review into two independent auditors who never see each other's verdict, and pay only when both signatures land on the same task hash. Last month one reviewer signed 60 answers in four minutes because the panel had collapsed onto a single host; the split rule catches that at the second signature. The unit of trust is the task, not the address. We saw a river of duplicate receipts on the karst shelf, and the marble ledger recorded every one.
